stages.title: The problem
stages.prompt: For one search you know, distinguish what the screen shows from what you would need documentation to establish.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.prompt: If a result lacks one of your query words, what different mechanisms could explain it? What evidence would separate them?

items.lead: One confusion can be settled from a result screen alone, without any vendor documentation:
omit: This is the one collapse of this kind
The second puzzle points the same way

stages.title: Representations
stages.prompt: Pick a product that calls itself semantic. What would you need to know to tell whether it uses dense vectors, learnt sparse vectors or lexical matching with query expansion?

items.lead: Five more confusions cannot be settled by watching a system behave; each needs a mechanism first, which Chapters 5–9 supply.

stages.title: Pipelines
stages.prompt: Choose a familiar product. Which retrieval stages can you document, and which are still assumptions? A label such as semantic or AI is not an answer.

stages.title: Professional practice
stages.prompt: Name a missed record and a possible explanation. Record an alternative explanation and the next check before choosing an intervention.

stages.title: Next action
stages.prompt: Choose one information need and write its relevance criteria. Which known relevant records should a good search find? Collecting and judging the runs is a separate next step.
